name: John Girder

tenures.source: the Dreamcard V card and the FWF's own singles ledger (promotions/dreamcard/archive/dreamcard-v-the-rising-sun-final-lineup-1992-04-16.html, promotions/fwf-1992/archive/fwf-singles-record-1993-01-08.html)

tenures.role: wrestler — one of the Mage's Gallery; winner of the second SuperCard's battle royal and World Heavyweight title challenger
tenures.source: the UFWS's own broadcasts, 18 July – 26 August 1991 (promotions/ufws/archive/pwgea-report-10-1991-07-18.html onward)
tenures.note: EXTENDED RATHER THAN DUPLICATED. The join is primary-source two ways: this federation's own ring announcer bills him at the second SuperCard as "the former EMWA World Champion and the winner of the Battle Royal," and the WeWF's own Summit of E-Wrestling update of 14 June 1991 lists "John Girder & Warren Hammer" under EMWA in its own by-federation entry list. Same man, two wings, one row.

tenures.source: the Summit of E-Wrestling's own broadcasts, served under that wing (promotions/summit-of-e-wrestling/holdings.html)

caption: The EMWA's own World Heavyweight Champion, put on the line against the FWF's at Dreamcard V and beaten by a disqualification his opponent engineered with a set of brass knuckles.
notes: Billed at Dreamcard V with a second, the Magician, whom no other held document names.

name: Brewster Cogburn
caption: An EMWA-original star credited by the community's own 1996 Hall of Fame process as one of the wing's earliest headliners, carrying the EMWA Intercontinental Championship before a long run through several other 1990s e-wrestling federations.

tenures.source: The rec.sport.pro-wrestling.fantasy community Hall of Fame and Museum's own 1996 nomination and inductee record (served under promotions/rspwf/archive/, msg_ids sXkgSjUeOHYJ 7 Jun 1996, lN8iu-CZGzEJ 30 May 1996, wYldxWD1A0IJ 10 Jun 1996, xofQ0iIY1akJ 30 Jun 1996 first-inductees announcement): "Cogburn got his start in the EMWA, the first e-wrestling federation, and remained a star for several years... He held titles in the EMWA and UFWS."

notes: A first-ballot 1996 Hall of Fame inductee (unanimous, all seven votes) per the same community record; also held the UFWS World Title, the EWC World Title and won the first Slick Ric Tournament at Summit Two, per the same documents — those other federations' own tenures are not re-derived here. The player who created and handled this character is named in the same source documents; that name is a standing, unrelated denial on the tree-wide ledger and is not repeated here (role only: "the character's own creator/handler").

identity.note: Same ring name as the held brewster-cogburn record in another wing; minted here from EMWA's own 1996 community Hall of Fame record with no evidence read this pass of the same handler or continuity — kept distinct pending a join test (coordinator, 2026-09-04).
